insights: Keep estimated code size separate from legal duplication: dynamic allocations, recursion, noduplicate operations, cross-block token uses and convergence are distinct dimensions.
InstructionCost is target-provided code-size cost, not a count of source nodes or a latency estimate. Backend lowering can turn source operations into different amounts of code.
Internal single-live-use callees and post-link-resolvable indirect calls are future inline opportunities; the model depends on pipeline stage rather than only present instruction count.

Collect proof/assumption-only ephemeral work through side-effect-free nonterminator dependencies and exclude it from executable cost only when all uses qualify. Ink fallible requires/ensures are executable checks, not removable assumptions.
Loop-local assumption filtering avoids repeating whole-function work per loop. Worklist uses an advancing index rather than shifting a vector; visited keys bound traversal.
The documented ephemeral analysis misses PHI-supported chains; treat estimated cost as conservative heuristics, not a correctness theorem or an optimal result.
GPU convergence is a control-dependency property in addition to ordinary memory effects. Generic duplication cannot infer safety from absence of writes alone.

Indirect branches/block-address references need cross-function identity handling; LLVM explicitly documents a conservative limitation. Ink source-bound closure and callback proofs should reuse exact dependencies.
Per-block cost sums and vector/return/inline counts can inform bounded family ranking, but require matched target measurements before selecting a generated application.
validation: Full source review, no local LLVM execution. No new cost model or semantic authority implemented from these observations yet.
